blocks.content:
Article 52 states that there shall be a President of India.
The President is the nominal executive (constitutional head), while the Prime Minister is the real executive.
The President is the nominal executive (constitutional head), while the Prime Minister is the real executive.

items: Article 52 mandates the creation of the office of the President of India.
Exams frequently test the distinction between the President (Nominal Executive) and the Prime Minister (Real Executive).

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Article 52 establishes the office of the President of India.
The President acts as the nominal executive or constitutional head of the nation.
The Prime Minister serves as the real executive authority.
